title: Tropical forest degradation monitoring
bottleneck: Deforestation gets the attention, but degradation — selective logging, understory fires, edge effects — may emit as much carbon while remaining nearly invisible to standard satellite monitoring: canopy cover persists while biomass and biodiversity collapse underneath. New radar and lidar methods can see degradation but lack the historical baselines and operational pipelines of deforestation tracking. REDD+ payments built on deforestation metrics miss most of the damage.
why_it_blocks: If degradation emissions are uncounted, forest carbon accounting is systematically wrong and conservation targets the wrong threat. The monitoring gap lets the largest forest carbon losses hide in plain sight.
current_state: GEDI lidar and new radar missions are mapping forest structure in 3D, promising degradation-sensitive monitoring. But operational, policy-ready degradation tracking integrated into carbon finance is still years away.
